title: Do plain-looking sim games really sell better? We checked 10 stores — November 2026 edition
lede: A viral post says indie developers should make simple-looking management, factory, colony and idle games instead of pretty ones. We re-scraped all ten stores we track and tested each claim against the numbers.
bottomLine:
Partly true, mostly on Steam, and not the way the post says. On Steam, sims do a bit better than the average paid game: 31% reach 100+ reviews, against 25% for all paid games. Colony, city-builder and factory games with 100+ reviews have some of the highest estimated sales of any genre. Idle and clicker games are the opposite: they rank last of 206 Steam tags.

The idea that players forgive plain art if they play for hours can't be tested, because no store we scrape publishes playtime. Ratings point the other way: sims are less often rated 85%+ positive than other games (41% vs 48% on Steam).

Outside Steam the advantage mostly disappears. Sims trail other games on PlayStation and Google Play and are level on GOG and Xbox. Roblox is the exception in volume: tycoon and simulator experiences are 30% of what we found there. They get better like-ratios than other experiences, but fewer visits.

For AnyGame: the useful part of the post is the method: find a genre where players stay a long time, then test a rough prototype for playtime before spending money. Do that with colony, city and factory games, not idle games. Expect the hard part to be the fun loop, as the replies said, not the art.
origin: On Nov 27, 2026 (9:17 AM ET), @froessell posted screenshots of an answer from Google's Gemini. It said to build "spreadsheet with graphics" sims (factory/automation, colony sim, management/tycoon, idle/incremental) on one reused engine across 2–3 games. The answer cites no sources. Its revenue numbers match published estimates: Chris Zukowski's analysis of VG Insights data for 2019 Steam releases, which found a median of about $1,136 lifetime and 68% under $10,000, and the "$1,100–$3,500" range on Steam Page Analyzer. The replies mostly agreed, with one caveat: balance and fun are still the hard part, and playtime is the number that matters.

claims.claim: (a) The median paid Steam game grosses about $1.1k–$3.5k lifetime; ~68% never reach $10k; ~4% pass $1M.
claims.evidence: Across 72,027 paid games, the estimated median is $2k–$7k. Between 56% and 70% stay under $10k, and 4.2%–7.3% pass $1M. For games released in 2019 (5,355 games, the same group Zukowski used): median $2k–$6k, with 68% under $10k at 30 copies per review. Our estimates sit a bit above the post's numbers, but the shape matches.

claims.claim: (b) These sim genres have the highest median revenue, $150k–$500k+ per title among games with 100+ reviews.
claims.evidence: The range is right for colony sims ($256k–$768k), factory/automation ($174k–$522k) and management/tycoon ($148k–$443k). But they are not the highest: Colony Sim ranks #18, City Builder #25 and Automation #42 of 206 tags, behind Moddable, Open World, Open World Survival Craft. Idle games fail badly: Idler ranks #203 and Clicker #206 ($31k–$92k).

For the 7,079 paid games in that band, the estimated median is $148k at 20 copies per review, $222k at 30 and $444k at 60. At 30 copies per review the middle half falls between $103k and $458k. So the post's range fits the upper half of games, at the higher multipliers. Price matters a lot: the median game in this band costs $11.99.

claims.claim: (d) Players forgive plain art if playtime is high (median 10h+, 85%+ positive).
claims.evidence: Playtime isn't in our data from any store, so the main point can't be tested. The ratings half points the other way. Among Steam games with 100+ reviews, 41% of sims are 85%+ positive, against 48% of all paid games. That compares with 62% for story-rich games and 66% for 2D platformers. Colony sims have the lowest share (40%). We can't measure whether art is 'plain'.

compIntro: A game counts toward a genre if that Steam tag is one of its 10 most-voted tags, so a game can appear in more than one row. Revenue ranges are estimates (see Method).
compNote: Estimated gross = reviews × 20 (low) to 60 (high) copies per review × list price. List price is the higher of the October and November prices, because 8,195 games were discounted when we scraped during Steam's autumn sale.
storesIntro: Each store has its own categories, so we mapped 'sim' separately for each one (the tags are listed under each store). Only some stores publish rating counts, so we compare sims with all other games on whatever signal each store has. Revenue estimates are Steam-only, because the review-to-sales rule only exists for Steam.
storesNote: Scores are converted to a share: stars/5 (App Store, Play, PlayStation, Xbox), GOG's 0–50 scale/50, Roblox like ratio. PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo, Epic and App Store tags come partly from keyword rules we wrote, so their sim groups are small and noisy. The App Store and Google Play data are chart and category samples, not full catalogs.

steam.text: The deepest data. Sims are 8.3% of the catalog. They get more reviews than other games (median 31 vs 22), and more of them reach 100+ (33% vs 26%). Their scores are a little lower. The top sims below are the genre's breakouts.

app-store.text: In our chart sample, idle and tycoon games have more ratings than other charting games (median 1,926 vs 622) and the same average stars. The sample only covers games already on the top charts, so this says sims that chart do well, not that sims chart more often.

google-play.text: On the category pages we scraped, sims have fewer ratings than other games (median 60,375 vs 149,388) and fewer installs (median band 1,000,000+ vs 10,000,000+). The sample is small (about 1,300 games).

playstation.text: Only 121 sims (0.9%). They have fewer ratings (median 105 vs 130), and far fewer are rated 85%+ (21% vs 42%). PC-style management games don't carry over well to console.

xbox.text: 188 sims. They have more ratings (median 49 vs 33), but the same share reaches 100+ (33%), and fewer are rated 85%+ (21% vs 33%).

nintendo.text: The eShop publishes no ratings. The only signal is its popularity rank, where sims are slightly more popular (median rank 8,065 vs 8,897). Most sims there are tycoon ports (RollerCoaster Tycoon and similar), and the sims below are sorted by popularity rank.

epic.text: No ratings or sales signal. Sims are 247 games (3.3%), median price $19.99 vs $14.99.

gog.text: GOG has the biggest share of sims (13.6%, using GOG's own Management, Managerial and Economic tags), but they do no better than other games: median 39 vs 45 ratings and the same average score. GOG's 'Management' tag also covers classic strategy games such as Heroes of Might and Magic.

itch.text: We only have itch's top-rated lists, with no counts. Idle, incremental and management games are 6.6% of what we found, and that share has been rising: 16% of 2026 entries vs 5% in 2020. That's interest from developers, not proof of sales.

roblox.text: Tycoon and incremental-simulator experiences are 30% of the 12,464 experiences we found. More of them are liked 85%+ (67% vs 39%), but their median visits are lower (1.8M vs 5.2M). The genre is crowded and free to play, which is the opposite of the post's model of paid $15–25 PC games.

timelineIntro:
Release years come from each store's listed release date (Roblox: the date the experience was created). These catalogs only include games still listed today, so older years undercount games that were removed. Our Steam catalog is SteamSpy's app list (~83k apps), which lags new releases, so 2025–2026 cover only part of what Steam actually released.

On Steam the sim share has roughly tripled: 3–5% of each year's releases from 2012 to 2019, 10% in 2021–2023, 11% in 2024 and 14% in 2025. In every year, the median sim got more reviews than the median other game (for example 106 vs 24 for 2018 releases and 23 vs 14 for 2023). The jump came in 2020–2021, after Factorio's 1.0 (Aug 2020) and Dyson Sphere Program (Jan 2021).
timelineNote: Each cell shows the number of sim releases and the sim share of that store's releases that year. The 2026 'combined' figure is mostly Roblox, whose catalog is built from what's trending now.

milestones.what: SpaceChem: an early 'programming as a puzzle' factory game
Hay Day: a farm and management game on mobile (13M+ ratings on Play today)
Zoo Tycoon (Xbox): a tycoon game on console
Banished: a solo-developer city/colony builder with plain art
AdVenture Capitalist (iOS) — idle tycoon goes mainstream on mobile; Steam version Mar 30, 2015
RimWorld 1.0: colony sim, plain top-down art, 212k Steam reviews
Factorio 1.0: the standard-setter for factory games, 194k reviews
Pet Simulator X created on Roblox (9.0B visits)

Dwarf Fortress on Steam (the 'spreadsheet sim' archetype)

Grow a Garden created on Roblox (36.0B visits)
The Farmer Was Replaced: a programming/automation idle game (in our shortlist)

milestoneNote: Dates are the release or 1.0 date each store shows today. Early Access start dates are often earlier (Factorio, RimWorld and Satisfactory were playable years before 1.0). Review and visit counts are from our Nov 27 scrape.
shortIntro: This is the screenshot's own filter: sim games released in the last 18 months (since May 28, 2025) with 300–2,000 Steam reviews, 85%+ positive, and no major publisher. A major publisher means one with 40+ titles in our catalog or one on a named list in the code; self-published games are always kept. Revenue is estimated at 20–60 copies per review.
shortNote: This list is short because few new games meet all four conditions. Survivorship matters: we only see games that already succeeded.
gapIntro: These are sets of three Steam tags (at least one a sim tag) where every pair exists in real games but no game has all three. They are ranked by how far they sit from the nearest real game (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 embeddings; lower = emptier). We checked 200,334 unused combinations. An empty spot is not proof anyone wants it: many are empty because the mix makes no sense. Look at the nearest real games before taking any of them seriously.
gapNote: The baseline nearest-match score for real games' own tags is about 0.83 (5th percentile), so everything here is emptier than 95% of real games.
soWhat:
• Use the method, not the numbers. Pick genres with long play sessions and loyal players (colony, city, factory). Build a one-screen prototype and measure how long people play before spending on art or the $100 Steam fee.
  • Avoid idle and clicker games on Steam. They rank last for estimated sales, and on mobile and Roblox they mostly win through free-to-play money-making, not $15–25 sales.
  • Ship on PC first. On consoles (PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo), sims are about 1% of catalogs and don't do better.
  • Fun and balance are the risk, not art. Sims are less often rated 85%+ positive, so players are hard on systems that don't work. Plan time for playtesting and balance.
  • Next step if you want it: measure real playtime for the shortlist from public sources (SteamSpy's playtime estimates or HowLongToBeat) and test the 10h+ claim directly.
method:
Data (all scraped Nov 27, 2026 with the same actors and inputs as October). Steam: collectivewin/steam-catalog-scraper 0.1.3, same input as the October run FwiVYa7CgChoV7Tpc. The first same-input run (9bBfwOliPCfx0mQeK, dataset w2KKxCu9X9J1mXpkV) stopped early because SteamSpy's app list kept failing ("Too many connections"). We then ran 24 runs of the same actor and build, each covering one page or chunk of the list. Where SteamSpy's list failed, we gave the run the October app list plus 45 freshly fetched SteamSpy pages and used the actor's own resume step, so it only enriched apps. Steam's store API failed for 8,709 apps; for those we kept fresh reviews and tags and took store fields (price, date, publisher, art) from October. Result: 83,468 apps. All run and dataset IDs are in refresh/runs-steam-2026-11-27.json.

The other nine stores used their October production batches, re-run with identical input, build and memory. Their run and dataset IDs are listed under each store above and in refresh/runs-other-stores-2026-11-27.json. Each store was normalized with its own tools/<store>/merge.py and derive_tags.py.

Revenue estimate (Steam only): reviews × copies-per-review × list price. We use 20, 30 and 60 copies per review, the range GameDiscoverCo (Simon Carless) reported for post-2020 Steam games (Aug 2020 and Nov 14, 2022 surveys; 2022 median about 29, and about 59 for games selling 50–100k copies). This is gross before Steam's 30% cut, refunds, taxes and discounts. It is an estimate, not sales data.

Gap engine: the same method as the October Steam run (tag triples, bge-small-en-v1.5, lowest nearest-neighbor similarity), limited to triples that include a sim tag. 75,021 of 83,379 game embeddings were reused from October because their text hadn't changed; the other 8,358 were re-embedded.
caveats:
• Gross revenue is estimated from reviews, never measured. Real multipliers vary from about 15 to 100+ copies per review.
  • Steam's 2025–2026 coverage is incomplete: SteamSpy's list lags new releases.
  • We scraped during Steam's autumn sale. Prices use the higher of the October and November values.
  • Steam's "Incremental" tag appears in our November data (236 games) but not in October's. We count it as idle.
  • PlayStation's first US batch failed (out of memory, as in October) after 400 rows. The next batch covered the rest of the US store, so coverage is similar to October. One GOG and one PlayStation country batch found nothing new.
  • Google Play's October Educational top-up (77 games, added locally) was not repeated.
  • Keyword-based tags (consoles, Epic, App Store) miss many sims and mislabel some. We dropped launchers (Roblox, Fortnite) from the top-game lists.
  • No store gives us playtime, so the central "playtime forgives ugliness" claim is untested.
sources:
• @froessell on X, Nov 27, 2026 (Gemini screenshots)
  • Chris Zukowski, "The median indie game does not earn a whole lot" (Nov 28, 2022, VG Insights data)
  • GameDiscoverCo, "Steam sales estimates: why game popularity matters!" (Nov 14, 2022) and "What's the real Steam reviews/sales ratio?" (Jul 19, 2020)
  • Steam Page Analyzer: "How much does the average Steam game make?"
  • Store data: Steam, App Store, Google Play, PlayStation Store, Xbox Store, Nintendo eShop, Epic Games Store, GOG, itch.io and Roblox public pages and APIs, via AnyGame's Apify actors.
